newsitem.title: Bosnia: Serbs to assert authority over Moslem villages.
newsitem.headline: Serbs to assert authority over Moslem villages.

text.p: Bosnian Serb police are to run joint patrols with international police to assert their authority over three villages recently reoccupied by Moslems, Bosnian Serb interior minister Dragan Kijac said on Tuesday.
Kijac announced the patrols after talks in the Serbs' mountain stronghold of Pale with Geoff Beaumont, who represents the United Nations envoy Iqbal Riza.

"The Interior Ministry and international police force patrols will enter the villages of Dugi Dio, Mahala and Jusici tomorrow, and by this act establish authority in this area which belongs to the Bosnian Serb Republic under Dayton," Kijac told reporters.

Beaumont confirmed the agreement, which would be the first formal patrols of the three villages since Moslem refugees last weekend moved back to their homes, damaged during the 3 1/2-year Bosnian war.

Last month almost 100 Moslems reoccupied the deserted village of Jusici under clauses in the Dayton peace accord which guarantee the freedom of movement and the right of refugees to return to their homes.
All three villages, including Jusici, lie in a strategicaly sensitive region on the Serb side of the demilitarised "zone of separation" which divides the former warring facitons.

After a series of tense negotiations, the Moslem settlers agreed to withdraw to a tented camp on the other side of the zone while international authorities processed their formal applications to return.
